root_cause: 65 fetch/spawn/while(true) sites in this tree have no bound, so a wedged Chrome, browser or CDP endpoint hangs the tool that is waiting on it instead of failing.

attempts.action: Added AbortSignal.timeout / timeout+killSignal to every flagged call across 30 files; replaced the while(true) pause-loop head with the structural cap; fixed the last multi-line call shapes (ffArgs/ffOpts, inline opts).
attempts.rationale: A hang is a defect of the launch, not a slow result: every wait must refuse at its own deadline.
attempts.predicted_outcome: fail_fast_audit --all-code findings 65 -> 0; the default scope (12 files) would have hidden them.
attempts.observed_outcome: files_scanned=103, total_findings 65 -> 0, verdict PASS, rc 0, wall 166.5 ms

root_cause: content-fix-test.cjs spent 8.16 s of 9.65 s IDLE on real timers, so the per-edit loop could not fit in seconds even though the suite asserts pure logic.

attempts.action: Installed _tools/test-clock.cjs into the suite host global (setTimeout/setInterval/Date/performance); settle() advances the timeline; the chrome stub answers on the real clock; poll loops bounded to 80x50 ms; beforeExit guard fails a run that stops before the final line.
attempts.rationale: The virtual clock already proved the same conversion on two suites; the third was what made the loop 9 s long.
attempts.predicted_outcome: content-fix wall 9353 ms -> under 1500 ms with ARMS 52/52.
attempts.observed_outcome: virtual clock 1033 ms PASS ARMS 52/52; KO_REAL_CLOCK=1 9297 ms PASS ARMS 52/52 (equivalence both ways)

attempts.action: First shipped shape: only content.js timers virtual, stub callbacks virtual, single drain per settle.
attempts.predicted_outcome: content-fix would run its 52 arms in order.
attempts.observed_outcome: FAILED: run ended after arm A with rc 0 (1 of 52 arms) - an unsettled await read as a pass; fixed by real-clock stub callbacks, 4-round flushReal convergence and the beforeExit guard

root_cause: The per-edit loop ran the two heaviest suites unconditionally (11.1 s), so an edit anywhere paid 11 s or the agent skipped verification.

attempts.action: New _tools/gate/fast-loop.mjs maps a changed product file to the suites that can falsify it, runs node --check for tool edits, refuses a wide diff (rc 2) and an unmapped code file (rc 1).
attempts.rationale: Landing runs everything once; the edit loop runs only what the edit can break.
attempts.predicted_outcome: twitch-adblock.js loop ~1.9 s, content.js loop ~1.2 s, and a 37-file diff refuses instead of measuring the box.
attempts.observed_outcome: twitch-adblock.js suites=3 wall=1880 ms PASS; content.js suites=1 wall=1218 ms PASS; 37-file diff refuted rc 2

root_cause: observability scored named/all-return-statements (75/654): 579 of those exits are pure value getters (return null, return m[1].toLowerCase()) that cannot and should not write a transition row, so the formula is unreachable by construction and the 11 it reports measures the denominator, not the tree.

attempts.action: Replace it with four measured facts: guard-shaped refusals that carry a row (census), state fields an arm references (census), suites with an anti-vacuity guard (grep), and hang-capable calls that are bounded (fail_fast --all-code). Same for inner_loop_speed: anchor the scale on the documented 15 s target (60) and the <=5 s goal (90) instead of 100*(1-s/15), which scored a COMPLIANT 7.5 s loop as 48.
attempts.rationale: A slider must be able to fail: the old observability formula cannot exceed 27 even if every refusal in the tree were named.
attempts.predicted_outcome: observability becomes a composite in 0..100 whose sub-facts each regress under mutation; inner_loop stops scoring compliant loops near zero; both RED arms prove the new formulas bite.
attempts.observed_outcome: observability 11 -> 45 as a four-fact composite (refusals 0/105 guards carry a row; state 38/68 fields referenced; suites 3/12 anti-vacuity; hang 0 findings/104 files), inner_loop_speed 48 -> 100 at 924.7 ms best-of-3 (samples 924.7/1035.6/1411.9) measured on the worst product file; overall 76.6 -> 87.4, delivery 58 and observability 45 the two below 90

root_cause: kick.com probes in content.js (kickPlaybackUrl, kickFetchDvr) and popup.js (kickStatus) had no AbortSignal, so a dark or wedged endpoint holds the popup/probe promise open forever and the user sees a spinner that never resolves.

attempts.action: Add AbortSignal.timeout(12000) to every kick.com probe in content.js/popup.js and 15000 to background.js's fetch, then prove the content.js suite still passes on the virtual clock (ARMS 52/52) and that the popup/background files parse.
attempts.rationale: A refusal at a deadline is the same law the tooling sweep applied, and a popup that waits forever is the user-visible form.
attempts.predicted_outcome: content-fix prints ALL CONTENT.JS FIX CHECKS PASSED with ARMS 52/52 at ~1 s; node --check clean on background.js/popup.js; fast-loop on content.js reports verdict=PASS.
attempts.observed_outcome: content-fix: ALL CONTENT.JS FIX CHECKS PASSED, ARMS 52/52 present, KO_VER 0.8.129 unchanged; node --check clean on background.js/popup.js/content.js; fast-loop --files content.js -> LOOP impacted=1 suites=1 syntax=0 wall=1416ms verdict=PASS

root_cause: A generated feature map (features/features.json, features/INDEX.md) goes stale the moment a new tool file lands, and the staleness is only visible as a gate FAIL (revival-features: unmapped file), so the fix must be a regeneration in the same wave as the tool, not a later cleanup.

attempts.action: Add the two new _tools files to the census by running feature_map_sync.py --repo . --gate immediately after the tools land, and commit the regenerated map beside them.
attempts.rationale: The map is projected from the tree; regenerating it in the same commit makes drift impossible to reach a landing without the gate naming it.
attempts.predicted_outcome: revival-features PASS with 0 problems and file_count _tools 58 -> 60
attempts.observed_outcome: feature_map_sync.py --repo . --gate -> {"verdict": "PASS", "problems": []}; _tools file_count 58 -> 60, tracked 157 -> 159; revival-features then reports 2 feature(s) match the tree

attempts.action: Re-synced features/INDEX.md + features/features.json after the archive file landed (the census gained docs/AGENTS-archive-2026-11-27.md), and kept the friction rail's own re-measurement of revival/FRICTION.json.
attempts.rationale: A generated map that does not name a new tracked document is stale the moment it lands; the drift row exists to force the sync into the same commit.

attempts.action: Re-ran feature_map_sync.py after the three new _tools files became TRACKED, so the _tools feature row names them (the pre-commit sync saw them as untracked and declared them nowhere).

root_cause: A recorded slider score goes stale or is written from a remembered number, so the record must be regenerated by the probe and committed with its evidence string in the same change; otherwise the scorecard is prose about prose.

attempts.action: Write benchmarks/sliders.json only through slider_scorecard.py set-many with --evidence naming the probe command and commit hash, then read it back with report --strict-evidence.
attempts.rationale: The scorecard's numbers are claims; the record must carry the command that produced them and be re-derivable in one run.
attempts.predicted_outcome: report --strict-evidence prints overall 94.1, unmeasured_sliders 0, and 8 rows each with an evidence string
attempts.observed_outcome: slider_scorecard.py report --repo . --strict-evidence -> overall_0_100 94.1, sliders_below_target 1 (delivery_balance 67), unmeasured_sliders [], every row carrying evidence 'node harness/twins/slider_probe.mjs --all --json (2026-11-27T07:33Z; commit 76ec690)'

root_cause: A slider row's number is a claim; recording eight rows with one shared evidence paragraph makes the file read as measured when it is one proof copied eight times, and --strict-evidence refuses it as duplicate_evidence.

attempts.action: Set each slider with its own evidence string naming that slider's own probe command and its own measured basis (node harness/twins/slider_probe.mjs --all -> per-slider proof field).
attempts.rationale: The scorecard's duplicate_evidence arm exists because the live file already did this once; distinct proofs are the only way the report can fail for a real gap instead of for copy-paste.
attempts.predicted_outcome: report --strict-evidence -> duplicate_evidence [] and unmeasured [], leaving exactly one honest gap (delivery_balance 67 < 90)
attempts.observed_outcome: slider_scorecard.py report --strict-evidence -> duplicate_evidence [], unmeasured_sliders [], gaps [('delivery_balance', 67, 90)]; the report now fails only on the honest product/meta ratio

root_cause: AGENTS.md accumulated 2790 lines of wave narrative beside its rules, so the delivery_balance hygiene sub-score (rulebook_lean, needs history elsewhere) was unreachable and the instruction projection stayed refused over its byte ceiling.

root_cause: A wall-clock metric whose command is the suite itself cannot tell a slow product from a busy box, so the acceptance rail reported a +183.8% regression on a box with all E-cores pinned and an empty product diff.

attempts.action: Moved the sampling half of the pre-flight into _tools/gate/load-sample.mjs (one instrument, two callers), added _tools/ko-timed-suite.mjs (BUSY/CANNOT -> typed latency_refused JSON, READY -> RESULT_MS=<suite wall with a bounded spawn>), pointed subsystem.ad_time_continuity_ms at it with parse_mode regex, and added gate check timed-suite (4 arms + the mutant that raises the ceilings).
attempts.rationale: benchmark_history already turns a typed latency_refused into CANNOT-MEASURE; the missing piece was that the metric's command never asked the box. A refusal is a reading, a raised tolerance is a lie.
attempts.predicted_outcome: metric_budgets rail PASS on a BUSY box with the ad metric CANNOT-MEASURE (not REGRESSED); on READY the same command prints RESULT_MS and grades normally; gate checks 33 -> 34.
attempts.observed_outcome: wrapper arms 14/14 PASS (busy refuses with total/busiest/pinned, cannot refuses naming the missing reading, ready prints RESULT_MS, failing suite propagates rc 7, mutant with ceilings 100 measures); sampler reads the refusal as 'starved: total=100% busiest=100% pinned=20 (ceilings total 70%, core 90%)' and parses RESULT_MS=7133 when ready; gate RESULT PASS checks=34 failed=0.

root_cause: The load pre-flight is advisory: ko-load-check printed BUSY and ko-guest.mjs started an 18-process guest anyway, so the watcher billed this pane 11.9% of the machine and the owner's freeze risk came from a launcher that never asked.

attempts.action: ko-guest.mjs calls readLoad() before spawning and refuses on BUSY/CANNOT-MEASURE with exit 3 and the reading, KO_ALLOW_BUSY=1 as the loud override, --dry-run to print the argv; new gate check guest-load-guard runs 12 checks / 4 arms that start nothing.
attempts.rationale: Advice in a log is not a limit; the artifact that starts the heavy step must be the one that asks whether it may, and the arms keep the refusal wired.
attempts.predicted_outcome: BUSY start exits 3 with the reading and no chrome spawned; KO_ALLOW_BUSY=1 proceeds and reports BUSY; READY launches; gate checks 34 -> 35.
attempts.observed_outcome: selftest 12/12 PASS arms=4/4; real busy arm 'guest not started: BUSY total=100% busiest=100% pinned=20' rc=3 with no chrome on the profile (0 procs); override dry-run proceeds reporting BUSY; gate RESULT PASS checks=35 failed=0.

root_cause: The ad path can only see playlists through the page's player worker; a live episode measured worker-hooked=NONE while worker-playlist=2, so an ad served in that episode would have been invisible and the ring could only say so afterwards.

attempts.action: Record KO-20261127-06 with the four episodes; the arm that makes it structural (an episode with the worker absent must write a worker-unhookable row naming evicted vs never-started) is specified but NOT yet written.
attempts.rationale: Naming the gap in the ledger is a record, not a fix; the rung stays where it is until the arm exists, and the SIM must not claim otherwise.
attempts.predicted_outcome: Ledger row present; no arm yet, so the failure stays preserved.
attempts.observed_outcome: KO-20261127-06 recorded (episodes=4, worker_hooked=[worker+worker x3, NONE], worker_playlist=2). NO arm yet: a fixture episode with the worker absent still produces silence, so the gap is named, not closed.
